newsitem.title: UK: Lower crude price weighs on UK oil shares.
newsitem.headline: Lower crude price weighs on UK oil shares.

text.p: Lower crude prices and lingering disappointment over results from Royal Dutch/Shell Group depressed oil stocks on the London Stock Exchange.

Shell Transport and Trading fell 15-1/2 pence to 992 after reporting lower third quarter earnings on Thursday. British Petroleum (BP), which is expected to announce a third quarter profit rise next week, fell 7-1/2 pence to 653-1/2.
BP is less skewed to poor refining and chemicals markets than Royal Dutch/Shell, therefore benefiting more from higher production results due to the recent strong oil price, analysts said.
Brent crude took a breather late on Thursday, falling about a dollar to $22.70 after the stock exchange had closed.
But prices were barely changed at this morning's open on London's International Petroleum Exchange.
Among pure production and exploration stocks, Enterprise Oil fell 13 pence to 543-1/2 and LASMO retreated 7-1/2 to 206-1/2.
Both were downgraded earlier this week by Salomon Brothers.
Analyst Gordon Gray said he saw little upside in the shares amid concerns over sustainability of crude oil prices.
